1.title: Securing AI Systems
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Securing A I Systems. This module opens Domain five, and covers task statement five point one. You will learn which A W S services and features protect identities, data, networks, agents and answers, and which security and privacy concerns the exam expects you to know. The exam gives you a threat or a need, and asks you to name the control.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Identify the A W S services and features that secure A I: I A M, K M S, Macie, PrivateLink, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, V P C, AgentCore Identity and Policy, and Guardrails. Describe source citation and data origins. Describe secure data engineering, and security and privacy considerations. And describe hallucination detection and grounding.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedar and Salt Hardens Its Assistant
1.text: At Cedar and Salt Travel, the security team reviews the booking assistant before launch. They ask: who can call the model, where does the data travel, and who can see guest data? The agent will also call a booking system for guests. And they ask how to prove where an answer came from. Your job is to choose the controls.

1.title: Shared Responsibility and Data Protection
1.text: Start with the shared responsibility model. A W S protects the infrastructure; you control your content, access and configuration. Amazon Bedrock model providers have no access to its logs, or to your prompts and completions. Use M F A, and I A M Identity Center or I A M, so each person gets only the permissions needed. Use T L S, where version one point two is required and one point three is recommended, plus A W S encryption. Log activity with A W S CloudTrail. And never put sensitive data in tags or free-form name fields. Exam tip: A W S secures the platform; you secure who can use it and what data goes in.

1.title: IAM: Roles, Policies and Permissions
1.text: I A M is the foundation of access control. An I A M role gives the application temporary credentials to call a model. An I A M policy allows only the needed actions, such as invoking one model. Least privilege means starting with no access and adding only what is required. Permissions boundaries and conditions limit what roles can do, and when. And separate roles can call models, manage guardrails and read training data. Exam tip: least privilege means roles with narrow policies, never shared long-term keys.

1.title: Encryption: AWS KMS and TLS
1.text: Encryption protects data in two states. In transit, T L S protects traffic to A W S services. At rest, data is encrypted with A W S K M S keys. A W S K M S creates and controls keys, which are held in hardware security modules and never leave K M S unencrypted. Use customer managed keys for control, with key policies that limit who can use them. Keys can protect Amazon S three data, guardrails, logs and knowledge base data stores. Key use appears in CloudTrail. Exam tip: encryption at rest with your own control of the key means A W S K M S customer managed keys.

1.title: Private Networks: Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink
1.text: A W S PrivateLink makes a private connection between your V P C and Amazon Bedrock. You reach Bedrock without an internet gateway, a network address translation device, a V P N or Direct Connect, and instances need no public I P address. You create an interface endpoint, with endpoints for the model runtime, agents and the control plane. An endpoint policy limits who can do what through the endpoint. And V P C security groups control traffic to your own resources. Exam tip: to keep model traffic off the internet, use a PrivateLink interface endpoint in your V P C.

1.title: Amazon Macie: Find Sensitive Data
1.text: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S three, by using machine learning and pattern matching. It finds P I I, financial information and credentials, and you can add custom identifiers. It also checks bucket security, such as public access, and creates findings. Use it on training data, R A G documents and logs stored in S three. Findings flow to EventBridge and A W S Security Hub. Exam tip: to find personal data hiding in S three files, use Amazon Macie.

1.title: Secrets Manager and CloudWatch
1.text: Four services support secure operation. A W S Secrets Manager stores, retrieves and rotates credentials and A P I keys, so none are hard-coded. Amazon CloudWatch provides metrics, logs and alarms, and receives Bedrock model invocation logs. Model invocation logging records prompts, responses and metadata; it is off by default, and delivers to S three or CloudWatch Logs. And A W S CloudTrail shows who called which A P I, for audits. Exam tip: no credentials in code means Secrets Manager, and an audit trail of prompts means invocation logging.

1.title: Securing Agents: AgentCore Identity and Policy
1.text: Agents need their own security controls. AgentCore Identity provides identity and credential management for agents. Agents act on a user's behalf, with secure access and audit trails. Policy in AgentCore sets rules, written in Cedar or in plain English, that are checked on every tool call at the Gateway. Policy runs outside the agent's code, so a manipulated agent cannot bypass it. Decisions are logged in CloudWatch for audits. Exam tip: who the agent is is AgentCore Identity, and what it may do is Policy in AgentCore.

1.title: Source Citation and Documenting Data Origins
1.text: Now data origins. Source citation means the answer shows which documents it used, so users can verify it. Data lineage is a record of where data came from and how it changed. Data cataloging is an inventory of datasets, with owners, meaning and sensitivity. On A W S, the A W S Glue Data Catalog and Amazon SageMaker Catalog hold catalog and lineage information. Knowledge Bases keep source attribution for R A G answers. And SageMaker Model Cards document a model's data and use. Exam tip: to prove where data or an answer came from, use lineage, cataloging and source citation.

2.title: Secure Data Engineering
2.text: This slide goes beyond the guide, with four secure data engineering practices. Assess data quality: check accuracy, completeness and freshness before use. Use privacy-enhancing technologies: mask, anonymize or tokenize personal data, and add statistical noise where suitable. Apply data access control: least privilege, and retrieve only what the user may see. And protect data integrity: prevent tampering with validation, versioning, encryption and audit logs. Exam tip: clean, minimal, protected and traceable data makes a safer A I system.

2.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
2.text: Match each concern to a control. Prompt injection: prompt design, the Guardrails prompt attack filter, and least privilege. Data leakage: the sensitive information filter, Macie, and no secrets in prompts. Output filtering and validation: Guardrails, schema checks and human review. Threat detection: Amazon GuardDuty finds unusual activity. Vulnerability management: Amazon Inspector scans for software flaws. Infrastructure protection: V P C, PrivateLink and security groups. Encryption: K M S at rest and T L S in transit. And audit trail and toxicity: invocation logs, CloudTrail and content filters. Exam tip: leakage points to Macie and filters, and injection points to Guardrails.

2.title: Hallucination Detection and Grounding
2.text: How do you detect hallucinations and improve accuracy? R A G grounding means answers come from retrieved, trusted documents. A contextual grounding check scores grounding and relevance against the source; below your threshold, between zero and zero point nine nine, the answer is blocked. Automated Reasoning checks validate answers against logical rules. Output validation checks format, facts and citations before showing an answer. And confidence scoring sends low-confidence answers to human review. Exam tip: for an ungrounded answer, use a contextual grounding check with a threshold, backed by R A G.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Securing AI Systems
2.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Which service: I A M, K M S, Macie, PrivateLink, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, V P C, AgentCore Identity or Policy, or Guardrails. Which concept: shared responsibility, source citation, data lineage or cataloging. Which practice: data quality, privacy-enhancing technologies, access control or integrity. Which concern: prompt injection, data leakage, output filtering, logging or toxicity. And which method: R A G grounding, output validation or confidence scoring. Exam tip: name the threat first, then the control.

2.title: Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Security Review
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and name the answer. Only the booking app may call the model: an I A M role with a least-privilege policy. Model traffic must stay off the internet: a PrivateLink interface endpoint. Encrypt knowledge base data with your own keys: a K M S customer managed key. Find guest emails in S three training files: Amazon Macie. Store the partner A P I key safely: Secrets Manager. Limit what the agent can do with the booking tool: Policy in AgentCore, with AgentCore Identity for the guest. Show where an answer came from: source citation, lineage and cataloging. And keep an audit trail of prompts: invocation logging and CloudTrail. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Access: shared responsibility, I A M least privilege, and AgentCore Identity and Policy. Data: K M S encryption, T L S, Macie discovery, Secrets Manager, quality and integrity. Network and logs: PrivateLink, V P C, CloudWatch, invocation logging and CloudTrail. Content: Guardrails, output validation, grounding and confidence scores. And origins: source citation, lineage, cataloging and Model Cards.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the customer when using Amazon Bedrock? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: controlling access and the data sent to models. A W S protects the infrastructure. Data centers, network cables and hardware are A W S's responsibility.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Cedar and Salt wants Amazon Bedrock traffic from its V P C to stay on the A W S network, with no internet gateway. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: an A W S PrivateLink interface V P C endpoint. It creates a private connection with no internet gateway, N A T device or public I P needed.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. Which two actions help prevent data leakage from an A I application? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Sensitive information filters mask P I I in prompts and responses, and Macie finds sensitive data in Amazon S three. Hard-coded keys, disabled encryption and public buckets increase leakage risk.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A team wants to limit which tools an agent may call and with what inputs, with rules enforced outside the agent's code. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It intercepts every agent tool call at the Gateway, and checks it against rules written in Cedar or natural language.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Which approach helps detect hallucinations in a R A G application by comparing answers with the retrieved source? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: apply a contextual grounding check with a threshold. It scores how well a response is grounded in the source and relevant to the query, and blocks responses below the threshold.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Which A W S service stores database credentials and rotates them, so they are not hard-coded in application code? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A W S Secrets Manager. K M S manages encryption keys, Macie finds sensitive data, and CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all six answers. Question one: B. Question two: A. Question three: A and C. Question four: D. Question five: C. Question six: B. That completes Module thirteen. Next, Module fourteen covers governance and compliance for A I systems.
